cards.summary: AP reports the strait remains effectively shut while the U.S. and Iran publicly differ over conditions for reopening.
detail: Associated Press reported on Aug. 11 that the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively shut and that Iran was insisting on conditions before reopening. The report said the dispute was still affecting the movement of crude and the wider regional security picture.

cards.summary: AP reported another modest pullback from U.S. records while oil remained volatile and Treasury yields eased.
detail: AP’s Aug. 11 market report said U.S. stocks slipped further from their records, with Treasury yields easing and oil prices swinging around uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz. The Russell 2000 rose 0.3% in the cited session.

The market signal is mixed rather than uniformly risk-off: strong earnings expectations have supported equities, while energy costs and geopolitical uncertainty complicate the inflation and growth outlook.
This is a dated market snapshot, not a forecast or recommendation. The next useful check is the next U.S. close alongside fresh oil and policy information.

cards.title: Oil and geopolitics keep the U.S. inflation channel in focus
cards.summary: Brent and U.S. crude rose in Asia’s Wednesday snapshot as the market waited for clearer evidence that Hormuz traffic can normalise.
detail: AP reported early Wednesday that Brent crude was up 0.9% at $89.67 a barrel and U.S. benchmark crude was up 0.9% at $83.98. The same report linked the move to doubts about when crude could flow freely through the Strait of Hormuz.

For the U.S. market, the relevant channel is the interaction between imported energy costs, inflation expectations, consumer purchasing power, and the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook. The direction is clear in the snapshot; the eventual economic effect is not.
The next evidence is a confirmed U.S. settlement, updated inflation data, and any official change in the shipping situation. This card is informational only.

cards.title: Korean chips lift Asia while oil remains higher
cards.summary: AP reported a 4% Kospi gain led by Samsung and SK Hynix, alongside mixed regional equities and higher crude.
detail: AP reported Wednesday that the Kospi gained 4% to 6,597.90, with Samsung Electronics up 7.7% and SK Hynix up 7.1%. The Nikkei rose 0.6%, the Taiex 0.8%, the Shanghai Composite 0.3%, while the Hang Seng fell 1.2%.

The regional move is concentrated rather than uniform: semiconductor buying drove Korea, while oil’s rise kept the geopolitical and inflation backdrop in view. A mixed regional index cannot be compressed into one Asia-wide trend.
Regional sessions close at different times, so these figures are a dated snapshot. The next update should confirm local closes and whether the chip rally broadens beyond the largest names.
